subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a core Gateway control-plane and per-agent runtime split, and what first milestone should be supported?
rationale: The remaining work requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, session-state, and migration boundaries; automation cannot safely choose those product and security contracts.

options.title: Approve phased runtime split
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow to execution placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the current scope and defer the broader Gateway split.

options.title: Defer core architecture change
options.body: Continue improving multi-gateway, worker, and plugin or harness slices without committing to a distributed runtime boundary yet.

recommendation.title: Approve phased runtime split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current-main and active-PR history on the inspected Gateway/runtime lifecycle surfaces.
